title: Draft: TCP: Isolated fragmented IP packet does not allow relative SEQ
description:
An isolated fragmented packet that is never reassembled is also
not handled well for the relative SEQ analysis.
Closes #13550.

added 2195 commits
  • bf01b221...c861454c - 2194 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 8a9c4fbc - TCP: Isolated fragmented IP packet does not allow relative SEQ
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7610/diffs?diff_id=638583793&start_sha=bf01b2211e857dcb6abc47f225b02413c8f1c22a)
changed title from **{-Draft-}: Isolated fragmented IP packet does not allow relative SEQ** to **{+TCP+}: Isolated fragmented IP packet does not allow relative SEQ**

What if the fragmented IP packet occurs before the base sequence numbers have been set? E.g., in the original capture in #13550, ignore all frames before 16.

Also, what if it is a short segment because the header wasn't entirely captured, but the sequence numbers are there? That could perhaps be the case if there are options, but it could be reasonable to set the sequence numbers (and base sequence numbers, if it's the first on the connection.) At this point in the packet, we do know that the sequence numbers are there in the header.

The crux here is: We need to check for setting the base sequence numbers before doing TCP sequence analysis, we only do sequence analysis if we have the segment length, and we need to adjust the sequence numbers to relative sequence numbers after doing sequence analysis (and we don't want to do any of those if it's in an error packet.)

So I think perhaps the best solution is -
1. Test for in error pkt, ignore these steps if so.
2. Check for setting the base sequence numbers
3. If not fragmented, test full header length, if so we have the segment length, record that, and do sequence analysis, recalculate window size and calculated next sequence number, if not add expert info.
4. Then adjust sequence numbers to relative if analysis and relative sequence numbers is turned on, even if we don't have the full header length or are fragmented.
